correctness.rationale: I wrote and executed a separate exact enumeration covering every one of the 1, 16 and 46,656 labelled profiles at n=1,2,3. For each bijection I used the intersection of two preference-prefix edge bitmasks as the blocking test; each unavailable blocking pair is excluded precisely when one side does not strictly prefer it. The same prefixes give zero-based ranks; the product uses n-r, not n+1-r. Every strict pair is oriented by actual E, with ties retained and counted separately. The enumeration reproduced the stable multiplicities 34,080/11,484/1,092 at three pairs; of 14,760 total pairs 8,304 have strictly ordered E and all corresponding product differences are positive. The eight cells (lower,upper;count;minimum) are (2,3;288;162), (2,4;144;243), (3,4;1656;54), (3,5;504;108), (3,6;24;189), (4,5;3096;9), (4,6;648;45), (5,6;1944;6). The remaining pair counts are 3,696 E-only ties and 2,760 ties in both. At two pairs both stable pairs tie on both scores; there is no comparison at one pair. All 24 bijections on the four-pair example give exactly the two displayed outcomes and rank vectors, with (7,4096) and (8,4608); the forcing argument in the repaired proof also checks. Any strict reversal by definition needs at least two stable outcomes. The known optimizer-set census is reproduced but no longer a claimed novelty.
residual_risks: The proof covers only n<=3 and the specific four-pair witness, not all profiles at four or any other utility normalization.

originality.rationale: Only the narrowed claim passes. The exact earlier matching boundary record has the same objectives, optimizer inclusion, optimizer counts and a four-pair reversal, but neither its statement nor its verifier establishes all strict pairwise comparisons. Global argmax inclusion imposes no order on the products of arbitrary nonmaximal alternatives, even leaving comparisons between equal-cost global minimizers and higher-cost outcomes open if several minimizers have different products. The additional quantified order is separately verified, and the new witness illustrates it at the known threshold with the minimum possible number of stable outcomes.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier pairwise tables or uninspected prior passages may exist. The bounded comparison establishes concrete coverage of the optimizer census, not absolute priority for the surviving pairwise theorem.

value.rationale: When ranking a menu of stable outcomes or applying an additional restriction that removes the unrestricted optimum, optimizer-set inclusion for that unrestricted set does not guarantee the relative ordering of the remaining outcomes. The all-pairs assertion still gives that comparison, with exact minimum differences and tie counts in the initial complete domain. The two-outcome example isolates the first obstruction without reliance on competing third outcomes. The utility of the repaired claim does not depend on repeating the older optimizer census.
residual_risks: The finite result does not establish empirical prevalence at larger sizes or effects of changing the positive cardinal utility model.
